evidence: Driven through the proxy on 2026-09-29 (tunnel egress from a US address). Every field was filled from vault tokens: first and last name, phone, country, ZIP, email, password and confirmation. Submit replaced the join form with a page whose heading contains "Welcome"; no challenge, no error, and no emailed-code step. The run report recorded identity, address, login_email and login_password fills and a created login. A "Welcome to Hilton Honors" mail carrying the member number reached the registered mailbox the same day. Selectors as discovered read-only on 2026-09-28 by scripts/signup-selectors.ts (session arm); each matched exactly one visible element.
gotchas: Phone is required: a country-code select (defaults to United States +1) beside a text input, input[name*="phone" i]. Fill it with the identity's national-number token. An identity with no phone on file cannot complete this form: the vault refuses the token.

Country/Region and ZIP are required. The country select is select[name*="country" i]:not([name*="phone" i]) (defaults to United States) and ZIP is input[name*="zip" i]; fill both from the address tokens.

A field filled with an empty value (an identity with no first or last name on file) is accepted by the fill and flagged only on submit: the form stays put with aria-invalid on those inputs and no page-level error. Check the identity carries names and a phone before starting.
Password rules: 8 to 32 characters, one uppercase, one lowercase, and one digit or special character. Pass maxLength 32 to create_login.
No emailed code at signup; the account is live on submit. The welcome mail, with the member number, is the owner's to read.
